system.name: HedraRAG
system.one_liner: a runtime system built on a graph-based abstraction (RAGraph) that coordinates generation and retrieval across heterogeneous RAG workflows

content.subject: how everyday, multi-hop, and knowledge-summary questions require increasingly complex retrieval-generation workflows

elements.name: LLM
elements.role: the generative model in the base RAG system, alternating with retrieval

elements.name: Vector Search
elements.role: the retrieval component in the base RAG system, alternating with generation

elements.name: External knowledge
elements.role: the knowledge store Vector Search queries

elements.name: Everyday question
elements.role: category heading for the simplest workflow, a single-hop factual question

elements.name: Document
elements.role: a retrieved passage feeding the generator; the basic unit reused in every workflow example

elements.name: Answer
elements.role: the generated response produced from retrieved documents

elements.name: Multi-hop reasoning
elements.role: category heading for questions requiring chained sub-questions and multiple retrievals

elements.name: Subquestion
elements.role: an intermediate question the workflow generates and retrieves for, decomposing the original multi-hop question

elements.name: Knowledge summary
elements.role: category heading for open-ended questions needing broad, iterative evidence gathering

elements.name: Question
elements.role: the original open-ended question driving iterative retrieval-generation (IRG)

relations.what: the LLM and Vector Search repeatedly hand off to each other
Vector Search queries external knowledge to fetch documents
retrieved documents are consumed by generation to produce an answer
a subquestion triggers a further retrieval

panels.label: Everyday question / One-shot
panels.differs: template: a single Document is retrieved once and a single Answer is generated once (1 retrieval, 1 generation)

panels.label: Multi-hop reasoning / Multistep
panels.differs: the question is decomposed into a chained Subquestion, each triggering its own Document retrieval, before a final Answer (2 retrievals, 3 generations)

panels.label: Knowledge summary / IRG
panels.differs: an open-ended Question drives more than 3 rounds of retrieving a Document and generating a partial summary, iterating until enough evidence is gathered (>3 retrievals and generations)

values.what: the worked example content for each workflow: actual questions, retrieved 'documents', and generated answers/summaries (e.g. 'Wilhelm Rontgen', 'June, 1516', 'Alexander Fleming')
values.linked_by: position along each row's left-to-right arrow chain, coloured by role (blue = question/answer text, green = document)
values.result_cells: each row ends in a boxed Answer (or, for IRG, an open-ended chain of Document/summary pairs) plus a caption naming the retrieval/generation count

content.key_idea: RAG workflows are heterogeneous: a one-shot question needs one retrieval and one generation, a multi-hop question needs chained sub-questions each triggering its own retrieval, and an open-ended summary needs more than three rounds of iterative retrieval and generation.
content.reading_order: top RAG-system loop first, then down the three rows, each read left (example question) to right (its workflow graph)

palette.used_for: pale blue fill of the LLM icon box and the Answer/Subquestion/Question text boxes
a deeper blue accent on borders/highlights of the blue boxes
pale green fill of the Vector Search icon box and every Document box
light gray fill of the three workflow-category boxes (Everyday question, Multi-hop reasoning, Knowledge summary)
very light gray background/border of the dashed workflow-example panels

style.stroke: dashed rounded-rectangle borders around each workflow example; thin black connecting arrows
style.arrows: thin black curved arrows linking question/subquestion/document/answer boxes; a double-line arrow linking Vector Search to External knowledge
style.font: sans-serif (Nimbus Sans/Arial), bold for box headers (Document, Answer, Subquestion, Question) and category names
style.icons: a head-with-gears LLM icon, a magnifying-glass Vector Search icon, a stack-of-books External-knowledge icon, plus a question-mark/lightbulb/book icon beside each workflow category

encoding.color_means: green marks retrieved Document boxes and the Vector Search icon; blue marks generated/asked text (Answer, Subquestion, Question) and the LLM icon; gray marks the three workflow-category boxes
encoding.line_style_means: solid curved arrows link a box to whatever it produces or triggers next; a double line shows Vector Search querying External knowledge; dashed rounded rectangles frame each workflow's worked example
encoding.state_means: not applicable; the three panels are alternative workflow shapes, not states of one instance
encoding.emphasis: the caption under each panel ('One-shot (1 retrieval, 1 generation)', ..., 'IRG (>3 iterative retrieval and generations)') names the escalating retrieval/generation cost so the three panels read as increasing complexity
reusable_patterns: a shared two-icon RAG-system overview (LLM <-> Vector Search <-> External knowledge) unpacked into concrete worked-example graphs for three workflow complexities, growing from a single Document/Answer pair to a chained sub-question graph to an open-ended iterative chain
weaknesses: node names repeat across panels ('Document 1', 'Answer') so without the dashed panel boundaries and captions the three examples could be misread as one connected graph

evidence: recent advances in RAG techniques have led to increasing heterogeneity in RAG requests
The number of stages often increases in workflows that perform multiple iterations of retrieval and generation
different tasks often adopt distinct workflow patterns by design

summary: Figure 1 motivates HedraRAG by showing how RAG workflows differ in structure and cost. At top, a generic RAG system alternates between an LLM and Vector Search over external knowledge. Below, three worked examples show increasing heterogeneity: an Everyday question ('Who got the first Nobel prize in physics?') is answered One-shot with a single Document retrieval and a single generated Answer; a Multi-hop reasoning question ('When did John V of Anhalt-Zerbst father die?') is solved Multistep by decomposing it into a chained Subquestion, each triggering its own Document retrieval, across 2 retrievals and 3 generations; and a Knowledge summary question ('Discovery of penicillin and subsequent impact') requires IRG, iterating more than 3 rounds of retrieval and generation while chaining documents into a running summary.
summary_zh: 该图示RAG工作流的异构性：顶部为LLM与向量检索交替的通用系统；下方三例复杂度递增——单跳问题仅需1次检索1次生成；多跳推理拆解子问题经2次检索3次生成；知识总结需迭代3轮以上检索生成，链接文档得出综述。
